title: Rust
tagline: Memory safety without a garbage collector
description: Rust from the first program to safe concurrency: Cargo, types and expressions, ownership, borrowing and slices, structs, enums and pattern matching, vectors, strings and hash maps, error handling with Result, modules and tests, generics and traits, lifetimes and trait objects, closures and iterators, smart pointers, threads, channels and shared state, and a complete command-line tool. Best after a first language; the C++ memory milestones make the ownership rules feel familiar. Practice compiles and runs in your browser.

milestones.title: First Steps
milestones.blurb: Cargo and your first program, variables and types, functions and expressions, control flow, and strings and input.

lessons.title: Rust and Cargo: Your First Program
lessons.summary: What Rust is for and what makes it different, installing it with rustup, creating and running a project with Cargo, the shape of a program with fn main, printing with println! and format strings, comments, and how to read the compiler's unusually helpful error messages.

lessons.title: Variables, Mutability and Types
lessons.summary: let and mut, why variables are immutable by default, shadowing, constants, the scalar types (integers of every size, floats, bool, char), type inference and annotations, integer overflow in debug and release builds, conversions with as and From, and tuples and arrays.

lessons.title: Functions and Expressions
lessons.summary: Declaring functions with typed parameters and return types, statements versus expressions, returning the last expression without a semicolon, blocks as expressions, early return, unit (), and why Rust has no function overloading or default arguments.

lessons.title: Control Flow
lessons.summary: if and else as expressions, loop with break values, while, for over ranges and collections, labelled breaks, a first look at match with ranges and multiple patterns, and choosing the right loop.

lessons.title: Strings and Input
lessons.summary: The two string types - owned String and borrowed &str - and when to use each, common string methods, building strings with push_str and format!, reading lines from standard input, parsing numbers with parse and handling failure, and a first taste of Result and unwrap.

milestones.title: Ownership and Data
milestones.blurb: Ownership and moves, references and borrowing, slices, structs and methods, enums, Option and match.

lessons.title: Ownership and Moves
lessons.summary: The three ownership rules, the stack and the heap, how String owns heap memory and frees it when dropped, moves versus copies, the Copy trait for simple values, clone for explicit deep copies, ownership through function calls and return values, and why this replaces both garbage collection and manual free.

lessons.title: References and Borrowing
lessons.summary: Using values without taking ownership - shared references &T and mutable references &mut T, the borrowing rules (many readers or one writer), why they prevent data races and invalid pointers, non-lexical lifetimes, dangling references the compiler refuses, and dereferencing with *.

lessons.title: Slices
lessons.summary: Borrowing part of a collection with slices - string slices &str and their byte ranges, array and vector slices &[T], ranges in indexing, slice methods (len, first, last, split_at, chunks, windows, contains, iter), mutable slices &mut [T], and writing functions that take slices to accept arrays, vectors and parts of them.

lessons.title: Structs and Methods
lessons.summary: Defining structs with named fields, tuple structs and unit structs, creating them with field init shorthand and update syntax, methods in impl blocks with &self, &mut self and self, associated functions like new, deriving Debug, Clone and PartialEq, and privacy with pub.

lessons.title: Enums, Option and match
lessons.summary: Enums whose variants carry data, methods on enums, matching with destructuring and exhaustiveness, Option instead of null and its everyday methods (unwrap_or, map, and_then, ?), if let and let else, and modelling states so invalid ones cannot be represented.

tasks.title: A robot driven by an enum

milestones.title: Collections, Errors and Modules
milestones.blurb: Vectors, UTF-8 strings, hash maps and sets, error handling with Result and ?, and modules, crates and tests.

lessons.title: Vectors
lessons.summary: Vec<T> in depth - creating with vec! and Vec::new, pushing, popping, inserting and removing, indexing versus get, iterating by reference, by mutable reference and by value, sorting and deduplicating, retain, extend and drain, capacity, and the borrow rules that apply to vectors.

lessons.title: Strings in Depth
lessons.summary: How Rust strings really work - UTF-8 bytes, chars and why there is no indexing by position, char_indices and safe slicing, building strings with push, push_str, + and format!, splitting, trimming and searching, case conversion, parsing, and converting between String, &str, char and bytes.

lessons.title: HashMap and HashSet
lessons.summary: Key-value lookups with HashMap - insert, get, contains_key, remove, iterating, and the entry API for counting and grouping - unique values with HashSet and its set operations, ordered alternatives BTreeMap and BTreeSet, ownership of keys and values, and which key types are allowed.

lessons.title: Error Handling with Result
lessons.summary: Recoverable errors with Result<T, E> and unrecoverable ones with panic!, handling results with match, unwrap_or, map_err and and_then, propagating errors with the ? operator, writing your own error enums with Display and std::error::Error, converting errors with From so ? works across types, Box<dyn Error> for quick programs, and when to panic.

lessons.title: Modules, Crates and Tests
lessons.summary: Organising code with mod, pub and use, privacy rules for items and struct fields, splitting modules into files, packages, library and binary crates, adding dependencies from crates.io with Cargo.toml, and writing unit tests with #[test], assert macros and cargo test, plus integration tests and documentation tests.

milestones.title: Generics, Traits and Lifetimes
milestones.blurb: Generic functions and types, traits, the standard traits, lifetimes, and trait objects.

lessons.title: Generics
lessons.summary: Writing code once for many types - generic functions with type parameters and trait bounds, where clauses, generic structs and enums like Option and Result, impl blocks for generic types and for specific types, const generics for array sizes, and monomorphization, which makes generics cost nothing at run time.

lessons.title: Traits
lessons.summary: Defining shared behaviour with traits, implementing them for your types and for existing ones, default methods, traits as parameters with impl Trait and generic bounds, returning impl Trait, associated types and constants, supertraits, the orphan rule, and blanket implementations.

lessons.title: The Standard Traits
lessons.summary: The traits every Rust type should know - Debug and Display for printing, Clone and Copy, PartialEq and Eq, PartialOrd and Ord for comparing and sorting, Hash for map keys, Default, From and Into for conversions, FromStr for parsing, and operator overloading with Add and friends - which to derive and which to write by hand.

tasks.title: A money type with standard traits

lessons.title: Lifetimes
lessons.summary: How the compiler makes sure references never outlive their data - what a lifetime is, lifetime annotations on functions like longest, the elision rules that let you leave most of them out, structs that hold references, lifetimes in impl blocks and methods, 'static, and practical ways out such as returning owned data.

lessons.title: Trait Objects
lessons.summary: Dynamic dispatch with dyn Trait - storing different types in one collection with Box<dyn Trait> and &dyn Trait, how vtables work, static versus dynamic dispatch and when to choose each, dyn-compatibility (object safety) rules, downcasting with Any, and enums as the alternative when the set of types is closed.

milestones.title: Closures, Iterators and Smart Pointers
milestones.blurb: Closures, iterator adapters, implementing Iterator, Box, Rc and RefCell, and pattern matching in depth.

lessons.title: Closures
lessons.summary: Anonymous functions that capture their environment - closure syntax and type inference, capturing by reference, by mutable reference and by value with move, the Fn, FnMut and FnOnce traits, passing closures to functions with generics or impl Fn, returning closures, storing them in structs and boxing them as dyn Fn.

lessons.title: Iterators and Adapters
lessons.summary: The Iterator trait and next, iter, iter_mut and into_iter, laziness, the common adapters (map, filter, filter_map, enumerate, zip, chain, take, skip, rev, flat_map, peekable, windows), consumers (collect, sum, count, fold, any, all, find, position, min_by_key, max_by), collecting into different types including Result, and why iterator chains are as fast as loops.

lessons.title: Implementing Iterator
lessons.summary: Writing your own iterators - a struct with state and a next method, getting every adapter for free, infinite iterators, iterators that borrow from a collection, IntoIterator so your type works in for loops, std::iter helpers (from_fn, successors, repeat, once), and extension traits that add your own adapters.

lessons.title: Box, Rc and RefCell
lessons.summary: Smart pointers - Box for heap allocation and recursive types, Deref and Drop, Rc for shared ownership with reference counting, RefCell for interior mutability checked at run time, Rc<RefCell<T>> for shared mutable data, Weak references to break cycles, and when each is the right tool.

tasks.title: A tree with Rc, Weak and RefCell

lessons.title: Pattern Matching in Depth
lessons.summary: Everywhere patterns appear (let, match, if let, while let, let else, function parameters, for loops), destructuring structs, enums, tuples, references and nested data, slice patterns, ranges, bindings with @, guards, ignoring with _ and .., refutable versus irrefutable patterns, and matches!.

milestones.title: Concurrency and Projects
milestones.blurb: Threads and channels, shared state with Arc and Mutex, async Rust, testing and tooling, and a complete command-line tool.

lessons.title: Threads and Message Passing
lessons.summary: Fearless concurrency - spawning threads and joining them, move closures that give a thread its data, scoped threads that can borrow, channels with mpsc for sending messages between threads, multiple producers, worker pools fed by a channel, and how Send and Sync let the compiler rule out data races.

lessons.title: Shared State with Arc and Mutex
lessons.summary: Sharing data between threads safely - Arc for shared ownership across threads, Mutex for exclusive access with lock guards, RwLock for many readers, atomics for counters and flags, avoiding deadlocks and holding locks briefly, poisoning, and choosing between message passing and shared state.

lessons.title: Async Rust
lessons.summary: An overview of asynchronous Rust - why async exists, futures and async fn, .await, why a runtime such as Tokio is needed, spawning tasks, running futures concurrently with join and select, async I/O, channels and timeouts, Send and 'static bounds on tasks, and choosing between threads and async.

lessons.title: Testing, Documentation and Tooling
lessons.summary: The Rust toolbox - cargo test with unit, integration and documentation tests, test organisation and fixtures, rustfmt and clippy, cargo doc and writing good doc comments, features and profiles, benchmarking, cargo workspaces, and publishing a crate.

lessons.title: Project: A Command-Line Tool
lessons.summary: Building a real command-line program in Rust - reading arguments with std::env::args and with clap, reading files or standard input, a library-plus-binary layout, one error type with exit codes, writing output efficiently, and the plan for the final project, a log summariser with filters.
